title: FedPEFT-IMU — Experimental Results

dataset.name: ucihar
dataset.description: waist smartphone accelerometer + gyroscope (50 Hz), 6 activities

encoders.name: limu_bert
encoders.pretrained_source: Official LIMU-BERT weights pretrained on HHAR (phones + smartwatches)

encoders.name: ssl_wearables
encoders.pretrained_source: Official Oxford harnet10 weights, self-supervised on UK-Biobank wrist data

encoders.name: unimts
encoders.architecture: ST-GCN, 10 graph blocks over a 22-joint skeleton, 64-512 channels
encoders.pretrained_source: Official UniMTS weights (motion-capture-synthesised IMU aligned with text)

encoders.name: halo
encoders.architecture: Patch-channel Transformer, 8 alternating temporal/channel layers, d=192
encoders.pretrained_source: Our re-implementation, self-supervised (MAE + patch contrastive) on the pool users

encoders.name: convgru
encoders.architecture: per-sensor 1-D conv + GRU(128), mean-pooled and concatenated (FedMultimodal style)

methods.name: fedavg_scratch
methods.label: FedAvg from scratch
methods.description: Random initialisation; the whole model is trained and uploaded every round.

methods.name: v0_full_ft
methods.label: V0 · Full fine-tuning
methods.description: Pretrained encoder; the whole model is fine-tuned and uploaded (upper-cost baseline).

methods.name: v1_head_only
methods.label: V1 · Head only
methods.description: Frozen pretrained encoder; only the heads g and h are trained and uploaded (lower-cost baseline).

methods.name: v2_lora_naive
methods.label: V2 · LoRA, naive avg
methods.description: LoRA (r=8) + heads; the server averages A and B separately: avg(B)·avg(A).

methods.name: v3_lora_exact
methods.label: V3 · LoRA, exact avg
methods.description: LoRA (r=8) + heads; exact FedEx-LoRA aggregation avg(B·A), residual folded into W0.

methods.name: v4_hetero_rank
methods.label: V4 · Heterogeneous ranks
methods.description: Device tiers train LoRA ranks 2/4/8; zero-pad, exact aggregation, SVD re-factorisation.

methods.name: v5_proposed
methods.label: V5 · FedPEFT-IMU (proposed)
methods.description: V4 + local norm + local input adapter + personal head + class-prototype alignment.

methods.name: v5_abl_no_local_norm
methods.label: V5 without local norm and input adapter
methods.description: V5, but the normalisation layers and the input adapter stay frozen (only the classifier is personal).

methods.name: v5_abl_shared_head
methods.label: V5 with a shared classifier
methods.description: V5, but the classifier is federated (shared) instead of personal; norm and adapter stay local.

methods.name: v5_abl_fixed_rank
methods.label: V5 with one LoRA rank (r = 8) on every device
methods.description: V5 without device tiers: every client trains rank 8 (exact aggregation + SVD as in V5).

methods.name: local_scratch
methods.label: Local training (no FL)
methods.description: Every client trains its own model from scratch on its own data; nothing is shared.

methods.name: ditto_scratch
methods.label: Ditto (personalised FL)
methods.description: Ditto (Li et al., ICML 2021), the basis of FedCHAR: a global FedAvg model plus a personal model per client, trained with a proximal term towards the global model.

methods.name: ditto_ft
methods.label: Ditto on the pretrained encoder
methods.description: Ditto starting from the pretrained encoder (V0 + a personal model per client): the strongest personalised full-model baseline, with the communication cost of V0.

findings: Under the published protocol, with α = 0.1, our best federated model (FedAvg, Conv-GRU) reaches a macro-F1 on the unseen test subjects of 0.899, against 0.798 for the best published federated result (FedOpt, FedMultimodal, Tab. 4); with α = 5, our best federated model (V0, ssl-wearables) reaches a macro-F1 on the unseen test subjects of 0.928, against 0.852 for the best published federated result (FedOpt, FedMultimodal, Tab. 4). Our re-run of the published FedAvg + Conv-GRU baseline (α = 0.1) scores 0.899 (published 0.775). Our re-run of the published FedAvg + Conv-GRU baseline (α = 5) scores 0.904 (published 0.788).

Centralized from scratch, HALO is the strongest architecture (macro-F1 0.957). Starting from the pretrained weights improves every encoder: LIMU-BERT +0.034, ssl-wearables +0.019, UniMTS +0.023, HALO +0.010 macro-F1.

Training from scratch in the federation (non-IID users, 20 % participation) loses LIMU-BERT 0.061, ssl-wearables -0.038, UniMTS 0.033, HALO 0.446, Conv-GRU 0.012 macro-F1 against centralized training from scratch. This is the gap the pretrained encoders are meant to close.

FedPEFT-IMU (V5) against full fine-tuning (V0), macro-F1: LIMU-BERT 0.928 vs 0.826 with 6x less uplink; ssl-wearables 0.954 vs 0.922 with 56x less uplink; UniMTS 0.920 vs 0.879 with 40x less uplink; HALO 0.847 vs 0.629 with 102x less uplink.

Federated LoRA without personalisation (best of V2/V3) against V0: LIMU-BERT V2 0.830 vs V0 0.826; ssl-wearables V2 0.902 vs V0 0.922; UniMTS V2 0.915 vs V0 0.879; HALO V3 0.739 vs V0 0.629. LoRA matches or beats full fine-tuning for LIMU-BERT, UniMTS, HALO; for ssl-wearables the frozen features need more than a low-rank update in this round budget.

Exact LoRA aggregation (V3) versus naive averaging (V2), macro-F1 difference: LIMU-BERT -0.016, ssl-wearables -0.012, UniMTS -0.064, HALO +0.013. On average exact aggregation is worse by 0.020. Exact aggregation must ship the dense residual to every client: downlink per round is LIMU-BERT 4x, ssl-wearables 34x, UniMTS 23x, HALO 10x that of V2.
Highest worst-10 % client F1 per encoder: LIMU-BERT V5 0.755; ssl-wearables V5 0.845; UniMTS V5 0.752; HALO V5 0.675; Conv-GRU Ditto 0.749.

New users, zero-shot (V5 = nearest global prototype; BatchNorm encoders first estimate their norm statistics from the new user's unlabelled windows): LIMU-BERT V5 0.881 vs V3 0.865; ssl-wearables V5 0.849 vs V3 0.927; UniMTS V5 0.805 vs V3 0.905; HALO V5 0.753 vs V3 0.710. On average the shared classifier of V3 transfers better to brand-new users than V5's prototype rule (-0.030); V5's advantage is on the devices that trained with it.

Transductive zero-shot (V5's prototypes first refined on the new user's unlabelled windows, no labels and no communication): LIMU-BERT 0.881 -> 0.899; ssl-wearables 0.849 -> 0.857; UniMTS 0.805 -> 0.905; HALO 0.753 -> 0.750.

For 1 of 31 federated models, 5 windows (12.8 s) of labels score below zero-shot. The models with the weaker half of zero-shot scores gain +0.089 on average from 5 windows (12.8 s) of labels, the stronger half changes by +0.038. The few-shot fit already corrects for its class-balanced sample, so the remaining loss suggests the classifier over-fits the few labelled windows per class; regularising it towards the global classifier is the next step.
Budget note: ssl-wearables, UniMTS, HALO ran with a reduced compute budget (see the callouts), so compare its methods with each other.
All numbers come from one user split (seed 0). Differences of a few F1 points should be confirmed with the 'full' profile (3 held-out lists) before they are claimed.
